paper_title: Exact solution of the frustrated Potts model with next-nearest-neighbor interactions in one dimension via AI bootstrapping (Yin, 2025, Physical Review Letters)

\section*{Claim}
For $q\geq 3$, $J_2=-1$, $k_B=1$, and $\beta:=1/T$, the zero-temperature asymptotics of the largest transfer eigenvalue are
\[
\lambda\sim
\begin{cases}
q-2, & J_1<0,\\
q-1, & J_1=0,\\
\sqrt{q-1}\,e^{\beta J_1/2}, & 0<J_1<2,\\
\dfrac{1+\sqrt{4q-3}}{2}\,e^{\beta}, & J_1=2,\\
e^{\beta(J_1-1)}, & J_1>2,
\end{cases}
\qquad (\beta\to\infty).
\]
Consequently the zero-temperature critical points are $J_1=0$ and $J_1=2$, and the corresponding residual entropies per spin are $\ln(q-1)$ and $\ln((1+\sqrt{4q-3})/2)$.

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}\quad &q\in\mathbb N,
\quad q\geq 3,
\quad J_2=-1,
\quad k_B=1,
\quad \beta:=1/T.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &x:=e^{\beta J_2}=e^{-\beta},
\quad y:=e^{\beta J_1/2}.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &u:=xy^2=e^{\beta(J_1-1)},
\quad w:=\sqrt{q-1}\,y=\sqrt{q-1}\,e^{\beta J_1/2},
\quad v:=x+q-2=e^{-\beta}+q-2.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\lambda:=\frac{u+v}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{u-v}{2}\right)^2+w^2}.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\text{If }\lambda=e^{\beta a}g(1+o(1))\text{ with }g>0\text{ independent of }\beta,
\text{ then }S_0=\ln g.
\end{aligned}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
For $J_1<0$,
\begin{align}
u&=e^{\beta(J_1-1)}=o(1),\\
w&=\sqrt{q-1}\,e^{\beta J_1/2}=o(1),\\
v&=e^{-\beta}+q-2=(q-2)(1+o(1)),\\
\lambda&=\frac{v+o(1)}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{-v+o(1)}{2}\right)^2+o(1)}\\
&=v(1+o(1))=(q-2)(1+o(1)).
\end{align}
For $J_1=0$,
\begin{align}
u&=e^{-\beta}=o(1),\\
w&=\sqrt{q-1},\\
v&=q-2+o(1),\\
\lambda&=\frac{q-2}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{q-2}{2}\right)^2+q-1}+o(1)\\
&=\frac{q-2}{2}+\sqrt{\frac{q^2-4q+4+4q-4}{4}}+o(1)\\
&=\frac{q-2}{2}+\frac{q}{2}+o(1)\\
&=(q-1)(1+o(1)).
\end{align}
For $0<J_1<2$, divide (P4) by $w$:
\begin{align}
\frac{u}{w}&=\frac{e^{\beta(J_1-1)}}{\sqrt{q-1}\,e^{\beta J_1/2}}
=\frac{1}{\sqrt{q-1}}e^{\beta(J_1/2-1)}=o(1),\\
\frac{v}{w}&=\frac{e^{-\beta}+q-2}{\sqrt{q-1}\,e^{\beta J_1/2}}=o(1),\\
\frac{\lambda}{w}
&=\frac{u/w+v/w}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{u/w-v/w}{2}\right)^2+1}\\
&=1+o(1),\\
\lambda&=\sqrt{q-1}\,e^{\beta J_1/2}(1+o(1)).
\end{align}
For $J_1=2$, divide (P4) by $e^{\beta}$:
\begin{align}
\frac{u}{e^{\beta}}&=1,\\
\frac{w}{e^{\beta}}&=\sqrt{q-1},\\
\frac{v}{e^{\beta}}&=e^{-2\beta}+(q-2)e^{-\beta}=o(1),\\
\frac{\lambda}{e^{\beta}}
&=\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+q-1}+o(1)\\
&=\frac{1+\sqrt{4q-3}}{2}+o(1),\\
\lambda&=\frac{1+\sqrt{4q-3}}{2}e^{\beta}(1+o(1)).
\end{align}
For $J_1>2$, divide (P4) by $u$:
\begin{align}
\frac{w}{u}&=\sqrt{q-1}\,e^{\beta(1-J_1/2)}=o(1),\\
\frac{v}{u}&=(e^{-\beta}+q-2)e^{-\beta(J_1-1)}=o(1),\\
\frac{\lambda}{u}
&=\frac{1+v/u}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{1-v/u}{2}\right)^2+(w/u)^2}\\
&=1+o(1),\\
\lambda&=e^{\beta(J_1-1)}(1+o(1)).
\end{align}
The dominant exponential rate changes where $J_1/2=0$ and where $J_1/2=J_1-1$:
\begin{align}
J_1/2=0&\iff J_1=0,\\
J_1/2=J_1-1&\iff J_1=2.
\end{align}
Using the multiplicative constants in the asymptotics and (P5),
\begin{align}
S_0(J_1=0)&=\ln(q-1),\\
S_0(J_1=2)&=\ln\left(\frac{1+\sqrt{4q-3}}{2}\right).
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\lambda\sim
\begin{cases}
q-2, & J_1<0,\\
q-1, & J_1=0,\\
\sqrt{q-1}\,e^{\beta J_1/2}, & 0<J_1<2,\\
\dfrac{1+\sqrt{4q-3}}{2}\,e^{\beta}, & J_1=2,\\
e^{\beta(J_1-1)}, & J_1>2,
\end{cases}
\quad S_0(0)=\ln(q-1),\quad S_0(2)=\ln\left(\frac{1+\sqrt{4q-3}}{2}\right).}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_5:
\section*{Claim}
For the special case $q=2$, $J_2=-1$, $k_B=1$, and $\beta:=1/T$, the zero-temperature asymptotics of the largest transfer eigenvalue are
\[
\lambda\sim
\begin{cases}
e^{-\beta}, & J_1<-2,\\
\varphi e^{-\beta}, & J_1=-2,\\
e^{\beta J_1/2}, & -2<J_1<2,\\
\varphi e^{\beta}, & J_1=2,\\
e^{\beta(J_1-1)}, & J_1>2,
\end{cases}
\qquad
\varphi:=\frac{1+\sqrt 5}{2}.
\]
Consequently the zero-temperature critical points are $J_1=-2$ and $J_1=2$, and each has residual entropy per spin $\ln\varphi$.

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}\quad &q=2,
\quad J_2=-1,
\quad k_B=1,
\quad \beta:=1/T.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &u:=e^{\beta(J_1-1)},
\quad w:=e^{\beta J_1/2},
\quad v:=e^{-\beta}.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\lambda:=\frac{u+v}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{u-v}{2}\right)^2+w^2}.\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\varphi:=\frac{1+\sqrt 5}{2}.\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\text{If }\lambda=e^{\beta a}g(1+o(1))\text{ with }g>0\text{ independent of }\beta,
\text{ then }S_0=\ln g.
\end{aligned}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
For $J_1<-2$, compare exponents:
\begin{align}
J_1-1&<-3<-1,\\
J_1/2&<-1.
\end{align}
Thus $u=o(e^{-\beta})$ and $w=o(e^{-\beta})$, while $v=e^{-\beta}$, so
\begin{align}
\lambda
&=\frac{e^{-\beta}+o(e^{-\beta})}{2}
+\sqrt{\left(\frac{-e^{-\beta}+o(e^{-\beta})}{2}\right)^2+o(e^{-2\beta})}\\
&=e^{-\beta}(1+o(1)).
\end{align}
For $J_1=-2$,
\begin{align}
u&=e^{-3\beta}=o(e^{-\beta}),\\
w&=e^{-\beta},\\
v&=e^{-\beta},\\
\frac{\lambda}{e^{-\beta}}
&=\frac{o(1)+1}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{o(1)-1}{2}\right)^2+1}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+1}+o(1)\\
&=\frac{1+\sqrt 5}{2}+o(1)=\varphi+o(1),\\
\lambda&=\varphi e^{-\beta}(1+o(1)).
\end{align}
For $-2<J_1<2$, compare $w$ with $u$ and $v$:
\begin{align}
\frac{u}{w}&=e^{\beta(J_1/2-1)}=o(1),\\
\frac{v}{w}&=e^{-\beta(1+J_1/2)}=o(1),\\
\frac{\lambda}{w}
&=\frac{u/w+v/w}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{u/w-v/w}{2}\right)^2+1}\\
&=1+o(1),\\
\lambda&=e^{\beta J_1/2}(1+o(1)).
\end{align}
For $J_1=2$,
\begin{align}
u&=e^{\beta},\\
w&=e^{\beta},\\
v&=e^{-\beta}=o(e^{\beta}),\\
\frac{\lambda}{e^{\beta}}
&=\frac{1+o(1)}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{1-o(1)}{2}\right)^2+1}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+1}+o(1)\\
&=\varphi+o(1),\\
\lambda&=\varphi e^{\beta}(1+o(1)).
\end{align}
For $J_1>2$,
\begin{align}
\frac{w}{u}&=e^{\beta(1-J_1/2)}=o(1),\\
\frac{v}{u}&=e^{-\beta J_1}=o(1),\\
\frac{\lambda}{u}
&=\frac{1+v/u}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{1-v/u}{2}\right)^2+(w/u)^2}\\
&=1+o(1),\\
\lambda&=e^{\beta(J_1-1)}(1+o(1)).
\end{align}
The dominant exponential rate changes where $J_1/2=-1$ and where $J_1/2=J_1-1$:
\begin{align}
J_1/2=-1&\iff J_1=-2,\\
J_1/2=J_1-1&\iff J_1=2.
\end{align}
At each of these two boundary points the multiplicative constant is $\varphi$, so by (P5),
\begin{align}
S_0(J_1=-2)&=\ln\varphi,\\
S_0(J_1=2)&=\ln\varphi.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{\lambda\sim
\begin{cases}
e^{-\beta}, & J_1<-2,\\
\varphi e^{-\beta}, & J_1=-2,\\
e^{\beta J_1/2}, & -2<J_1<2,\\
\varphi e^{\beta}, & J_1=2,\\
e^{\beta(J_1-1)}, & J_1>2,
\end{cases}
\quad J_{1,c}\in\{-2,2\},\quad S_0(J_{1,c})=\ln\varphi.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_6:
\section*{Claim}
For $q\geq 4$ in the large-$q$ low-temperature approximation, with $J_2<0$ and $J_1>-2J_2$, comparing the free energies of the ferromagnetic, randomly dimerized, and paramagnetic zero-temperature sectors gives
\[
k_BT_{F\to D}=\frac{J_1+2J_2}{\ln(q-1)}
=\frac{J_1+2J_2}{\ln q}\left(1+O\!\left(\frac{1}{q\ln q}\right)\right),
\]
\[
k_BT_{D\to P}=\frac{J_1}{2\ln(q-2)-\ln(q-1)}
=\frac{J_1}{\ln q}\left(1+O\!\left(\frac{1}{q\ln q}\right)\right).
\]
Consequently the paper's large-$q$ estimates are $k_BT_{F\to D}\approx(J_1+2J_2)/\ln q$ and $k_BT_{D\to P}\approx J_1/\ln q$, with $0<T_{F\to D}<T_{D\to P}$ for sufficiently large $q$.

\section*{Premises}
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{(P1)}\quad &q\geq 4,
\quad q\text{ is large},
\quad J_2<0,
\quad J_1>-2J_2,
\quad k_B>0.\\
\text{(P2)}\quad &\text{Ferromagnetic sector: }E_F=-J_1-J_2,
\quad S_F=0.\\
\text{(P3)}\quad &\text{Randomly dimerized sector: }E_D=-J_1/2,
\quad S_D=\frac{1}{2}\ln(q-1).\\
\text{(P4)}\quad &\text{Paramagnetic sector: }E_P=0,
\quad S_P=\ln(q-2).\\
\text{(P5)}\quad &\text{Low-temperature sector free energies are approximated by }f_A\approx E_A-k_BT S_A.\\
\text{(P6)}\quad &\text{A crossover temperature between sectors }A\text{ and }B\text{ is estimated by }f_A=f_B.\\
\text{(P7)}\quad &\ln(1-r/q)=-r/q+O(q^{-2})\text{ for fixed }r\text{ as }q\to\infty.\\
\text{(P8)}\quad &\text{For sufficiently large }q,\quad D_q:=2\ln(q-2)-\ln(q-1)>0.
\end{aligned}
\]

\section*{Derivation}
Using (P2)--(P5), the three low-temperature free-energy approximations are
\begin{align}
f_F&\approx -J_1-J_2-k_BT\cdot 0=-J_1-J_2,\\
f_D&\approx -\frac{J_1}{2}-k_BT\left(\frac{1}{2}\ln(q-1)\right),\\
f_P&\approx 0-k_BT\ln(q-2)=-k_BT\ln(q-2).
\end{align}
For the $F\to D$ crossover, impose $f_F=f_D$:
\begin{align}
-J_1-J_2&=-\frac{J_1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}k_BT_{F\to D}\ln(q-1) &&\text{by (P6)},\\
-2J_1-2J_2&=-J_1-k_BT_{F\to D}\ln(q-1) &&\text{multiply by }2,\\
k_BT_{F\to D}\ln(q-1)&=J_1+2J_2 &&\text{rearrange},\\
k_BT_{F\to D}&=\frac{J_1+2J_2}{\ln(q-1)}.
\end{align}
For the $D\to P$ crossover, impose $f_D=f_P$:
\begin{align}
-\frac{J_1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}k_BT_{D\to P}\ln(q-1)&=-k_BT_{D\to P}\ln(q-2) &&\text{by (P6)},\\
-J_1-k_BT_{D\to P}\ln(q-1)&=-2k_BT_{D\to P}\ln(q-2) &&\text{multiply by }2,\\
k_BT_{D\to P}\bigl(2\ln(q-2)-\ln(q-1)\bigr)&=J_1 &&\text{rearrange},\\
k_BT_{D\to P}&=\frac{J_1}{2\ln(q-2)-\ln(q-1)}.
\end{align}
Now expand the logarithmic denominators.  By (P7),
\begin{align}
\ln(q-1)&=\ln q+\ln(1-1/q)\\
&=\ln q-\frac{1}{q}+O(q^{-2}),\\
\frac{1}{\ln(q-1)}&=\frac{1}{\ln q}\left(1+O\!\left(\frac{1}{q\ln q}\right)\right).
\end{align}
Similarly,
\begin{align}
2\ln(q-2)-\ln(q-1)
&=2\bigl(\ln q+\ln(1-2/q)\bigr)-\bigl(\ln q+\ln(1-1/q)\bigr)\\
&=\ln q+2\left(-\frac{2}{q}+O(q^{-2})\right)-\left(-\frac{1}{q}+O(q^{-2})\right)\\
&=\ln q-\frac{3}{q}+O(q^{-2}),\\
\frac{1}{2\ln(q-2)-\ln(q-1)}&=\frac{1}{\ln q}\left(1+O\!\left(\frac{1}{q\ln q}\right)\right).
\end{align}
Substitution gives the large-$q$ estimates
\begin{align}
k_BT_{F\to D}&=\frac{J_1+2J_2}{\ln q}\left(1+O\!\left(\frac{1}{q\ln q}\right)\right),\\
k_BT_{D\to P}&=\frac{J_1}{\ln q}\left(1+O\!\left(\frac{1}{q\ln q}\right)\right).
\end{align}
Finally, (P1) gives $J_1>0$ and $J_1+2J_2>0$.  Also, for sufficiently large $q$,
\begin{align}
0&<D_q=2\ln(q-2)-\ln(q-1)<\ln(q-1),\\
0&<J_1+2J_2<J_1.
\end{align}
Therefore
\begin{align}
0<T_{F\to D}
&=\frac{J_1+2J_2}{k_B\ln(q-1)}\\
&<\frac{J_1}{k_B\ln(q-1)}\\
&<\frac{J_1}{k_BD_q}=T_{D\to P}.
\end{align}

\section*{Final Result}
\[
\boxed{k_BT_{F\to D}=\frac{J_1+2J_2}{\ln(q-1)}\sim\frac{J_1+2J_2}{\ln q},\qquad k_BT_{D\to P}=\frac{J_1}{2\ln(q-2)-\ln(q-1)}\sim\frac{J_1}{\ln q},\qquad 0<T_{F\to D}<T_{D\to P}.}
\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
